faqs.a: Both use the same core math, but this calculator adds compounding-frequency choice (monthly, quarterly, annual) and is built around an investing mindset: initial stake plus recurring contributions. Future value is the pure math version.
faqs.q: How is this different from the Future Value calculator?

faqs.a: Yes - set the initial amount to 0. The whole result then comes from monthly contributions compounding over time, which is exactly how most people invest.

Monthly compounding applies one-twelfth of the annual rate each month. Quarterly applies one-fourth every three months. The differences are small but real: more frequent compounding always wins slightly, which is why this calculator lets you switch.
faqs.q: Monthly vs quarterly vs annual compounding?

faqs.a: Contributions are assumed at the end of each compounding period. Monthly contributions are grouped to match the period you pick: for quarterly compounding, each quarter gets 3 months of contributions.
faqs.q: When are contributions assumed to be made?

faqs.a: Because real returns vary year to year and this calculator assumes one fixed rate. Use a conservative 5-6% for planning and compare with 8-10% to see the range of possible outcomes.
faqs.q: Why would my real investment differ?

faqs.a: No. This is a planning projection, not a prediction or a recommendation. It ignores which assets to buy, when to rebalance, taxes, and fees. Talk to a licensed professional before investing real money.

investment-calculator.formula:
Periods per year p = 12, 4, or 1; period rate r = annual rate / p; periods n = years x p
Payment per period = monthly contribution x 12 / p
FV = initial x (1+r)^n + payment per period x ((1+r)^n - 1) / r
Contributions = initial + monthly contribution x 12 x years
Growth = FV - contributions
howTo: Choose the compounding frequency: monthly, quarterly, or annual.
Enter your initial investment (0 to start from scratch).
Enter the expected annual return and the number of years.
Read the future value, your contributions, and the growth separately.
keyFacts: Investing growth = your deposits plus compounding on those deposits.
More frequent compounding grows slightly faster.
Contributions usually dominate early; compounding dominates late.
The growth row shows exactly what compounding earned you.
A fixed rate is assumed - real markets fluctuate.
